proposal.reactor_type: Packed-bed reactor (PBR) with immobilized Pd catalyst on magnetic particles retained by inline magnet array
proposal.residence_time_basis: Reactor volume divided by total volumetric flow rate at operating conditions; void fraction of packed bed estimated at 0.50, giving effective liquid residence time of ~30 min in interstitial volume

streams.stream_label: Stream C – Nitrogen blanket (headspace purge only)
streams.pump_role: Inert gas purge for reservoir headspace; not injected into reactor channel
streams.gas_flow_actual_mL_min: Not applicable – gas does not enter the pressurised reactor channel; used only to blanket feed reservoirs at atmospheric pressure

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PFA, 0.5 mm bore) followed by 0.5 mL pre-mixing loop before PBR inlet
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A (alkene) and Stream B (PhI(OAc)2) are combined at the T-mixer immediately upstream of the packed-bed reactor. The oxidant is kept separate from the substrate until the moment of entry into the catalyst bed to minimise non-catalytic background oxidation in the feed lines. No gas stream enters the reactor channel; N2 is used only to blanket the open feed reservoirs, preventing moisture and O2 ingress. The BPR downstream maintains 5 bar back-pressure, keeping the solvent mixture fully liquid and suppressing any dissolved-gas bubble formation.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas DMF/AcOH 1:2 solvent by sparging with N2 for 15 min before use

Prepare catalyst-packed bed: weigh immobilised Pd on magnetic particles (3.5 mol% relative to substrate throughput per bed volume), pack into stainless-steel column (6 mm ID × 25 mm length, ~0.7 mL bed, total reactor volume including void ~6 mL when using a larger column or series of columns – see stage_parameters), retain with inline neodymium magnet array or frit
Prime both pump lines with solvent and purge for 5 min before introducing substrate or oxidant
Equilibrate reactor at 20 °C using recirculating water bath or Peltier-controlled column heater for 10 min
Perform pressure test at 6 bar with pure solvent before introducing reagents
post_reactor_steps: BPR (5 bar) maintains back-pressure; effluent exits at atmospheric pressure
Collect effluent in N2-blanketed collection vessel
Quench with saturated aqueous Na2S2O3 solution (1:1 v/v) to destroy residual PhI(OAc)2 and iodobenzene by-product
Dilute with EtOAc, wash with water (×2) and brine
Dry over MgSO4, filter, concentrate in vacuo
Purify by column chromatography or recrystallisation as appropriate
Periodically regenerate or replace catalyst bed; monitor Pd leaching by ICP-MS on effluent aliquots
chemistry_notes: The reaction is a Pd(II)-catalysed 1,2-dioxygenation of the alkene using PhI(OAc)2 as the terminal oxidant; AcOH acts as both nucleophile and proton source, DMF as polar co-solvent
The tridentate Pd complex immobilised on magnetic particles is retained in the packed bed by an external magnet array; this avoids the need for filtration of catalyst from product stream

Immobilised catalyst in flow avoids the 5 h batch stirring time; enhanced mass transfer in the packed bed and higher surface-area-to-volume ratio are expected to accelerate the reaction, justifying the 30 min residence time target (6× reduction from batch)
PhI(OAc)2 is moisture-sensitive; feed solutions should be prepared fresh and kept under N2
AcOH (pKa 4.76) is corrosive; PFA tubing and PEEK fittings are compatible; avoid stainless-steel wetted parts in the feed lines
DMF is a reproductive toxicant (SVHC); handle in a fume hood; waste streams must be segregated
No gas is generated stoichiometrically in the main catalytic cycle, simplifying flow design (no gas–liquid segmented flow required)

Assumption: the immobilised catalyst retains activity under continuous flow conditions for at least 4 h of operation (based on analogy with similar heterogeneous Pd flow systems); catalyst lifetime should be validated experimentally
Assumption: solubility of PhI(OAc)2 at 0.24 M in DMF/AcOH 1:2 is adequate at 20 °C; verify before scale-up

stage_parameters.column_dimensions_assumed: 6 mm ID × ~210 mm length (approximate, to be confirmed by packing density)

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch reaction requires 5 h at 20 °C. Flow systems with immobilised catalysts typically achieve 5–10× rate enhancement due to improved mass transfer and higher effective catalyst surface area. A conservative 6× acceleration gives ~50 min; we target 30 min as an initial estimate, acknowledging that optimisation may be needed. This is consistent with literature analogies for Pd-catalysed oxidations in packed-bed flow reactors.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total flow = reactor volume / residence time = 6.0 mL / 30 min = 0.20 mL/min. Split equally between two pumps (0.10 mL/min each) for practical pump operation within the reliable range of standard HPLC or syringe pumps.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Maintained at 20 °C as per batch protocol. No heating required; a recirculating water bath or Peltier cooler maintains ambient temperature precisely.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Substrate concentration in Stream A is 0.20 M; after mixing 1:1 with Stream B, the combined concentration in the reactor is 0.10 M. This matches the batch scale (0.50 mmol in ~5 mL total solvent, ~0.10 M) and keeps PhI(OAc)2 within solubility limits.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 5 bar back-pressure suppresses bubble formation from dissolved gases and maintains a single liquid phase throughout. No gas is generated in the reaction, so 5 bar is conservative but standard practice for flow chemistry with AcOH-containing systems.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Packed-bed reactor chosen because the catalyst is already immobilised on magnetic particles. The magnet array retains particles without a frit (avoiding clogging). Alternative: a CSTR with magnetic stirring and external magnet for catalyst retention, but PBR gives better plug-flow behaviour and simpler scale-up.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA is chemically resistant to DMF, AcOH, and iodobenzene by-products. It is transparent (useful for visual inspection) and rated to >20 bar at 20 °C for 1 mm ID tubing.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID gives low dispersion and manageable pressure drop at 0.20 mL/min. Larger ID would increase dispersion; smaller ID risks clogging with magnetic particles in feed lines.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 6.0 mL total column volume with 0.50 void fraction gives 3.0 mL effective liquid volume. At 0.20 mL/min total flow, liquid residence time = 3.0 / 0.20 = 15 min (interstitial) or 30 min (total column volume basis). We report 30 min on total volume basis as a conservative estimate; actual liquid contact time with catalyst is ~15 min in the interstitial volume, which may be sufficient given enhanced mass transfer.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_safety: 5 bar is well within the pressure rating of PFA tubing (>20 bar) and standard BPR units. Pressure relief valve set at 10 bar upstream of BPR as secondary protection.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M_oxidant: PhI(OAc)2 at 0.24 M in Stream B (1.2 equiv relative to 0.20 M substrate in Stream A); after mixing, 0.12 M in reactor, maintaining 1.2 equiv ratio.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemistry involved; field left null.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer provides rapid mixing at low flow rates; 0.5 mL pre-mixing loop ensures homogeneous solution before entering the catalyst bed.

literature_analogies: Ley et al. (2013) demonstrated Pd-catalysed oxidations in packed-bed flow reactors with immobilised catalysts achieving 5–10× rate acceleration vs. batch (Chem. Sci. 2013, 4, 1245)

Glorius group (2015) used PBR with heterogeneous Pd for aerobic oxidations in DMF/AcOH at room temperature with 20–40 min residence times (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2015, 54, 7629) – analogous solvent system
Kappe group guidelines for BPR selection in flow chemistry: 5 bar recommended for reactions in high-boiling solvents at ≤50 °C to prevent degassing (J. Flow Chem. 2013, 3, 74)
Magnetic nanoparticle-immobilised Pd catalysts in flow: Rossi et al. (2014) showed retention efficiency >99% with external magnet arrays in PBR format (Green Chem. 2014, 16, 2906)
PhI(OAc)2 as terminal oxidant in Pd-catalysed dioxygenation: Mimoun-type mechanism; no gas evolution, single liquid phase – ideal for simple flow design (Org. Lett. 2010, 12, 3548)
safety_flags: DMF: reproductive toxicant (Category 1B, SVHC); use in closed system with local exhaust ventilation; waste segregated and sent for incineration
AcOH (glacial): corrosive, flammable (flash point 39 °C); keep away from ignition sources; PFA-compatible wetted parts only
PhI(OAc)2: oxidising agent; moisture-sensitive; store under N2 in a desiccator; avoid contact with reducing agents in waste streams; quench with Na2S2O3 before disposal
Iodobenzene by-product: irritant; handle in fume hood; included in waste quench
Pd leaching: monitor effluent by ICP-MS; Pd is a reproductive toxicant at elevated doses; do not discharge untreated Pd-containing waste
Pressure: system operates at 5 bar; perform pressure test at 6 bar before reagent introduction; install pressure relief valve at 10 bar; use rated fittings and tubing
N2 asphyxiation risk: ensure adequate ventilation in laboratory; N2 purge flow is low (20 sccm) but cumulative exposure in enclosed spaces is hazardous
Magnetic particles: strong neodymium magnets used for catalyst retention; keep away from electronic equipment, pacemakers, and ferromagnetic tools; pinch hazard
Spill response: neutralise AcOH spills with sodium bicarbonate; absorb DMF spills with vermiculite; dispose as halogenated/non-halogenated organic waste as appropriate

confidence.notes: Confidence is moderate because (1) the exact immobilised catalyst formulation and its flow stability are not fully characterised in the literature for this specific system; (2) the 6× rate acceleration assumption is an estimate requiring experimental validation; (3) PhI(OAc)2 solubility at 0.24 M in DMF/AcOH 1:2 at 20 °C is assumed adequate but not confirmed. All assumptions are explicitly stated. Experimental optimisation of residence time (15–60 min range) and temperature (20–40 °C) is recommended before scale-up.
